conviction_note: Sum of three findings (+2.0 germanium, -0.8 locked earnout charge, -0.8 buried cost-plus supply-back) nets to +0.4; the two negatives are GAAP/margin items this shareholder base has demonstrably looked through (Feb-2026 print rallied 21.5% on a GAAP loss), while the germanium tape is a real fundamental divergence from a 28% beta-driven drawdown, so the honest answer is a small positive tilt with very wide dispersion, not conviction.

findings.finding: Germanium printed 26,500 CNY/kg on 2026-09-10, up 8.16% in the past month and up 84.03% year over year, i.e. the squeeze that is the entire economic case for LightPath's germanium-free BlackDiamond glass accelerated through exactly the June quarter and through the 20 days in which LPTH fell 27.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing the germanium input, LPTH would have decoupled from the drone complex during the August unwind. It did not: on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-28 LPTH fell alongside Ondas, Unusual Machines, Red Cat and Kratos - names with zero germanium exposure and opposite YTD performance - which is the signature of positioning, not of anyone re-underwriting LightPath's input economics. A market that had priced this would show LPTH's 20-day beta to the c-UAS basket breaking down and 25-delta skew tilted to calls; instead skew is +1.21 vol points (mildly put-bid) and the stock tracked the basket point for point. Ge substitution is also the specific mechanism management named as the order driver on 2025-09-25, so the call has a live, quantifiable hook the tape is ignoring.
findings.independence: China's suspension of its gallium/germanium/antimony export ban to the US expires 2026-11-27 - eleven weeks after this print - a hard dated cliff that raises the urgency of qualifying germanium-free optics: https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/library/news/china/2025/11/china-251109-globaltimes04.htm (URL path /2025/11/ confirms the November 2025 announcement, not a relabelled story). Separately, the July 2026 $11M follow-on c-UAS camera order explicitly includes a planned migration of that customer from germanium optics to BlackDiamond: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lightpath-technologies-receives-11-million-follow-on-order-for-infrared-cameras-from-leading-global-technology-customer-302825901.html

findings.finding: An April 16, 2026 side letter fixed the G5 Infrared Year-2 earnout at exactly $9.0M ($6.3M cash + $2.7M stock, payable 1-15 January 2027) against a carried liability of only $6.7M at 31 March 2026 - so roughly $2.3M of additional non-cash fair-value/accretion charge is arithmetically locked into the Q4 FY26 P&L, on top of the $1.78M Amorphous Materials earnout accrual, guaranteeing a GAAP loss materially wider than the single published ($0.02) estimate and a $6.3M cash outflow four months out.
findings.why_not_priced: With a single published EPS estimate on the name and no sell-side model visible that reconciles the side letter, the headline GAAP number that hits the wires and the algos at 16:05 ET is pre-determined to look like a large miss versus ($0.02). If this were priced there would be a visible adjusted-vs-GAAP bridge in the previews and the estimate itself would sit nearer ($0.06)-($0.09); instead the aggregators still carry ($0.02). The offset - and why I size this small rather than large - is that this base has looked through identical earnout noise before: the 11-Feb-2026 print carried a fair-value charge and the stock rose 21.5%.
findings.independence: Independent read of the same side letter by a buy-side writer, published 2026-05-13, noting the Year-2 earnout was locked at the $9M maximum and that the earnout was creating $3.4M of non-cash charges and $3.8M of operating cash impact per quarter: https://cupofcoffeecapital.substack.com/p/lightpath-q3-2026-breakdown . Note this and the 10-Q are two readings of the same underlying document - treat as one source cluster.

findings.finding: Buried in the body of the 22 July 2026 8-K on the China divestiture - not in the press release and not in any wire story - is a five-year supply-back obligation under which the divested Zhenjiang plant sells product to LightPath at cost plus a markup that starts at 10% and steps up 5 points for every $1M of the $4.5M purchase price the buyer repays, capped at cost plus 30%, so LightPath's own input cost rises mechanically as it collects its sale proceeds.
findings.why_not_priced: Every wire item on this deal reported the same three facts - $4.5M price, five-year installments, management buyer, 'fully Western-aligned footprint' - and none reported the markup escalator. The press release exhibit itself discloses only that China contributed ~$4.5M of third-party revenue and is silent on cost of goods. Zhenjiang was the in-house low-cost molded-optics plant supplying the Visible Components line at internal cost; converting that to cost+10% rising to cost+30% is a structural gross-margin headwind against management's stated 40% target, which they were already guiding as slipping 'a quarter or 2'. If the market had read the agreement, the 40% margin bridge would be being questioned in previews; it is not being mentioned at all.
findings.independence: Corroborating on the other side of the same transaction, the 23 July 2026 press release quantifies only the revenue that leaves ($4.5M/yr of third-party sales) and says nothing about cost: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/889971/000143774926024234/ex_991571.htm . Separately, management's own margin-slip language on the 7 May 2026 call: https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/markets-news/Motley%20Fool/1808770/lightpath-lpth-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ . The 8-K body and its exhibit are one filing - one source cluster.

searched_and_found_nothing: SEC filing tape for a fresh catalyst behind the 27.9% drawdown: no 8-K since 2026-07-23 and no Form 4 since 2026-06-04, so nothing company-specific triggered it

Whether the China sale has closed - no 8-K item 2.01 and no closing press release seven weeks after 'expected to close in the coming weeks'; too weak to size, but it also means held-for-sale/discontinued-ops presentation at 30 June is uncertain rather than a reliable revenue-reclass surprise
Held-for-sale write-down math: AOCI was a +$1.29M credit at 31 March 2026, so a Zhenjiang disposal recycles a small gain, not a loss - the impairment angle I went looking for is not there

Short interest as a squeeze setup: the only figures I could source (114,200 shares) are inconsistent with the baseline's 3.4M ADV and look stale, so I dropped the angle rather than cite a number I cannot date

The August 2026 investor deck on lightpath.com/hubfs is a 6.7MB PDF that would not render in any tool available here - potentially the single most valuable unread document on this name and I could not open it

Analyst consensus revenue for FY2026: one search summary implied a stale $61.9M against $50.56M already booked in nine months, but Simply Wall St returned 403 and I could not date the figure, so no finding
Job postings and LinkedIn for a hiring inflection: 39 open roles across the group, but no dated prior baseline to compare against, so unusable
USAspending / prime-contractor award notices naming LightPath, Visimid or G5 Infrared in the June-September window: nothing new beyond the already-wire $11M July order
baseline_tension: My net finding is mildly positive and therefore cuts against the -27.9% run-up, but not against the option market - the 25-delta skew is only +1.21 vol points and the put/call OI ratio 0.75, i.e. the chain is close to balanced, so I am disagreeing with the momentum and with nobody's explicit bet; the drawdown itself is corroborated as a c-UAS-complex positioning unwind (Ondas, Unusual Machines, Red Cat and Kratos fell together on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-28) rather than a statement about this company's quarter, which is why I do not treat the run-up as information here.
